KEN.note: A NASA satellite crop-productivity measure feeds a child malnutrition forecast, a health use and not a farming service.
Nothing on rules or an authority for AI harms.
The only AI tool is a health sector forecast, which belongs to the sectoral study.

facts.fact: The research team (USC, Microsoft, Amref Health Africa and the Kenyan health ministry), writing in The Conversation, says its machine learning model forecasts child acute malnutrition one month ahead with 89% accuracy and a prototype dashboard exists, which the team is working with the ministry to make available to local decision-makers.

systems.owner: Ministry of Health with research team

KEN.note: The model was built by a mainly foreign research team; no local build, AI computing or sharing with named users is stated.
No tier, point of digitisation or share of primary clinics is stated.

facts.fact: The research team says the Kenya Health Information System, built on DHIS2, holds monthly facility clinical data from across Kenya (January 2019 to February 2024) that the health ministry has collected for many years.
